name: Penedès & Cava

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Grenache, Cabernet Franc, Tempranillo, Dolcetto and Merlot fully without cooking off their freshness.
Garnacha sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.
Chardonnay is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 5°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.

sheet.place: Penedès sits southwest of Barcelona, from the sea up to about 800 m inland. The climate is warm and Mediterranean, and the soils are limestone, marl and sandstone.
sheet.rules: Cava is made by the traditional method, with a second fermentation in the bottle. Cava needs 9 months on the lees, Reserva 18, Gran Reserva 30 and Paraje Calificado 36. Macabeo, Xarel·lo and Parellada are the classic grapes.

claims.claim: DO Penedès is a Mediterranean wine area in Catalonia, southwest of Barcelona. Its vineyards run from near sea level to about 800 m inland.
The traditional three-way split is Baix Penedès (Penedès Marítim, near the sea), Penedès Central or Mitjà (the plain between), and Alt Penedès (Penedès Superior, inland against the mountains).

Baix Penedès is the lowest and warmest zone because of the sea. Alt Penedès is the highest and coolest, with bigger day-night swings, more frost and more rain. The Central zone mixes both climates and, in Guía Peñín's account, supplies much of the grapes for cava.
Parellada is the traditional grape of the cooler, high Alt Penedès. Xarel·lo and Macabeo dominate the Central zone, where much goes into cava.

Today the DO also uses a 2015 soil-based subzone map with around ten zones, such as Marina del Garraf, Costers del Montmell, Alts d'Ancosa and Massís del Garraf i Costers de l'Ordal. The older three-zone split is no longer how the DO describes itself.

Overall climate is Mediterranean, mild and warm. Zone average temperatures run from about 11-14 C in Alts d'Ancosa (coldest) to 16-17 C on the Garraf coast (warmest). Rain runs from about 500 mm on the coast to about 650 mm inland.

Soils vary by zone. Common types are shallow young soils on steep slopes, deeper soils on gentle slopes and valley floors, and calcium carbonate build-up. Parent rocks include Cretaceous limestone, marl and dolomite (Garraf and Ordal), slate and granite (Anoia hillsides) and sandstone and marl (Lavernó hillsides).

The DO specification names three geological units: the Garraf Massif, the pre-coastal Penedès Depression, and the inland mountain range between Montserrat and the Montmell. Low ground has Miocene sandstone and marl from alluvial fans at the foot of the mountains.
Guía Peñín describes Penedès soils as deep and permeable, a balance of sand and clay, poor in organic matter and not very fertile.
Montserrat is the jagged mountain to the north of the Penedès. The DO specification uses it as one end of the inland range (Montserrat to Montmell) that frames the Penedès basin.

DO Cava is not tied to one place. Official zones are Comtats de Barcelona, Valle del Ebro, Viñedos de Almendralejo and Requena (Levante). The Barcelona zone is Catalan Cava and has five subzones: Valls d'Anoia-Foix, Serra de Mar, Conca del Gaià, Serra de Prades and Pla de Ponent. The Ebro zone has Alto Ebro and Valle del Cierzo.
The Consejo Regulador says Cava began in the Penedès, especially in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia and around it, and calls the town the capital of Cava.

Nearly all Cava is made in Catalonia, mostly in the Penedès, and Sant Sadurní d'Anoia alone is said to make most of it. Reported figures are more than 90 to 95% from the Penedès and over 75% from Sant Sadurní.

Cava de Guarda Superior (Reserva, Gran Reserva, Paraje Calificado) has stricter rules: organic grapes, vines older than 10 years, and a maximum yield of 10,000 kg/ha. Organic was to be mandatory by 2025.
Cava is made by the traditional method. The base wine is bottled with yeast and sugar, a second fermentation happens in the bottle, and the wine then ages on its lees.

Nine grapes are authorised. White: Macabeo, Xarel·lo, Parellada, Chardonnay, Subirat Parent. Red: Garnacha, Trepat, Monastrell, Pinot Noir. Macabeo is the most planted, then Xarel·lo, then Parellada. Together those three are the classic Cava blend.
Cava (Cava de Guarda) must age at least 9 months on the lees.
Reserva needs at least 18 months of ageing. It is part of Cava de Guarda Superior.
Gran Reserva needs at least 30 months of ageing.
Paraje Calificado needs at least 36 months of ageing, and comes from a single named plot and estate-made wine that passes a tasting committee.
The Consejo and press describe these as time in the bottle, and the lees contact is the same period. Counted from tirage (bottling for second fermentation).
